newsitem.title: CROATIA: Police seize another Mostar warlord in Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Police seize another Mostar warlord in Croatia.

text.p: Croatian police have arrrested another Bosnian Croat warlord in what appears a coordinated crackdown on organised crime in Croat-held southern Bosnia, state news agency HINA reported on Friday.
"Police officers arrested Vinko Martinovic aka Stela on February 26 in the (southern Croatian) Dalmatian area," HINA quoted an Interior Ministry statement as saying.
It said Martinovic was seized "on a well-founded suspicion that he was involved in committing a criminal act liable to official prosecution".

Identical wording, without specifying the nature of the crime, was used by police on Wednesday, after they arrested Mladen Naletilic Tuta, the paramount mafia leader in the southern Bosnian city of Mostar.

Naletilic and Martinovic have been explicitly accused by Western mediators of being at the centre of a powerful mafia cartel that runs western, Croat-controlled Mostar and opposes international efforts for a stable peace in the region.
While Naletilic was arrested on Monday during a routine police car control in a village near Croatia's border with Bosnia, Martinovic temporarily escaped arrest.
The captures were seen as a major policy turnabout for the nationalist government of President Franjo Tudjman, the ultimate patron of the Bosnian Croats.
Croatian authorities have in the past appeared to tolerate, if not protect, the rogue elements in western Herzegovina who oppose normalising relations with Bosnian Moslems.
The Foreign Ministry in Zagreb said on Friday Croatia "welcomes the measures Bosnian Croats have taken in surpressing crime and opposition to the (Croat-Moslem) Federation.
"Croatia has also given firm support to those measures," the statement, faxed to Reuters said.

Analysts believe the arrests resulted from pressure Western diplomats put on Tudjman to get rid of Mostar gangsters after two attacks on NATO-led peacekeeping troops in Mostar last week, when armoured vehicles were targeted with anti-tank missiles in the Croat part of town.
Bosnian Croat police in Mostar on Wednesday seized five more men, all Croats, for armed robbery and issued arrest warrants for another three.
The spokesman for the High Representative to Bosnia, Colum Murphy , said in Sarajevo he believed altoghether 19 men had been arrested so far.

He also said West Mostar's deputy police chief, identified by an International Police report to have opened fire on a group of Moslem civilians earlier this month, had gone missing and was being sought.
One Moslem civilian was kiilled in the incident and over twenty wounded. The IPTF report identified several Croat policemen as firing on the crowd and urged Mostar officials to prosecute them.
